entries.name: CasLimits
entries.signature: export type CasLimits = { /** Nodes of the input tree, and of each output tree before printing. Default 5 000. */ readonly nodes: number; /** Nesting depth of the input tree. Default 10 000. */ readonly terms: number; /** Degree in any one generator, checked before powers and products. Default 1 000. */ readonly degree: number; /** Degree of the inputs of a polynomial gcd. Default 64. */ readonly gcdDegree: number; /** Digits of any coefficient, estimated before multiplying; also the precision cap of π/e sign decisions. Default 1 000. */ readonly digits: number; /** Arithmetic steps per call. Default 100 000. */ readonly fuel: number; /** Highest derivative order, checked before differentiating. Default 10. */ readonly order: number; /** Steps of one derivation, bounded before each order from the size of what it differentiates. Default 2 000. */ readonly steps: number; /** Printed nodes across a derivation's steps, counted before any step is printed. Default 50 000. */ readonly stepNodes: number; /** Degree of each square-free part `factor` splits over ℚ. Default 128. */ readonly factorDegree: number; /** Digits of the largest coefficient `factor` splits over ℚ. Default 300. */ readonly factorDigits: number; /** Digits of the modulus p^k that Hensel lifting reaches, computed before lifting. Default 2 000. */ readonly liftDigits: number; /** Candidate products tried while recombining modular factors. Default 65 536. */ readonly recombination: number; };

entries.name: derivative
entries.signature: export declare function derivative(input: Expr, variable: string, options?: DerivativeOptions): CasResult; ; export declare function derivative(input: CasInput, variable: string, options?: DerivativeOptions): CasResult | CasTextFailure;
entries.jsdocSummary: The derivative of `input` with respect to `variable`; every other name is a constant (a partial derivative). Higher orders are normalized between orders. `conditions` lists where the result holds: the input's restrictions the result no longer shows (`ln(x)` → `1/x` needs `x > 0`, reason `domain`) and the points where a rule needs more (`abs(x)` → `sign(x)` needs `x ≠ 0`, reason `differentiable`).

Default 1; at most the `order` budget (default 10). */ readonly order?: number; /** False returns the last order's raw derivative (`fold` applied only) instead of the readable normal form. Default true. */ readonly simplify?: boolean; };

entries.name: exactRoots
entries.signature: export declare function exactRoots(form: PolynomialForm, options?: CasOptions): ExactRoots;
entries.jsdocSummary: Closed-form roots of a `polynomialIn` result: rational and quadratic-surd roots over ℚ, and roots in ℚ(π, e) and its square roots for π/e coefficients (`pi*x = 1` → `1/pi`). A quadratic whose discriminant's sign the `digits` budget cannot decide goes to `numeric`. Zero-testing assumes π and e are algebraically independent (standard, unproven; see the README).

entries.name: ExactRoots
entries.signature: export type ExactRoots = { /** Closed-form roots; `real: false` for complex ones, which print with `i`. */ readonly roots: readonly { readonly value: Expr; readonly multiplicity: number; readonly real: boolean; }[]; /** Parts with no closed form here, ascending float coefficients, for a numeric solver. */ readonly numeric: readonly { readonly coefficients: readonly number[]; readonly multiplicity: number; }[]; /** False when `numeric` is non-empty. */ readonly exact: boolean; };

entries.name: expand
entries.signature: export declare function expand(input: Expr, options?: CasOptions): CasResult; ; export declare function expand(input: CasInput, options?: CasOptions): CasResult | CasTextFailure;
entries.jsdocSummary: Products and integer powers of sums multiplied out; like terms collected. A quotient comes back as one fraction, cancelled by the gcd (the `rationalize` form). Kernels (`sin(x)`, `sqrt(x)`) stay atoms.

entries.name: factor
entries.signature: export declare function factor(input: Expr, variable: string, options?: CasOptions): Factored; ; export declare function factor(input: CasInput, variable: string, options?: CasOptions): Factored | CasTextFailure;
entries.jsdocSummary: `input` as content times a product of factors in `variable` (RFC §8.2). Rational coefficients are factored completely over ℚ by Zassenhaus's algorithm; every factor returned is proven irreducible, and a budget that runs out (`factorDegree`, `factorDigits`, `liftDigits`, `recombination`) throws `CasLimitError` instead of returning a partial answer.

entries.name: Factored
entries.signature: export type Factored = { /** The constant factor: a rational, or for coefficients in other names, π or e, the part without the variable. */ readonly content: Expr; /** Factors in the variable, by degree then text, each with coprime integer coefficients and a positive leading coefficient. */ readonly factors: readonly { readonly factor: Expr; readonly multiplicity: number; }[]; /** * True when every factor is irreducible. Each square-free part with * rational coefficients (after the content, which may hold other names, π * or e) is factored completely over ℚ. A part whose coefficients still * involve other names, π or e stays whole, and `complete` is false (v1 has * no multivariate factoring), unless it has degree 1 in the variable: such * a part is primitive, so it is irreducible (`x^2 + 2xy + y^2` is * `(x + y)^2`, complete). */ readonly complete: boolean; /** Restrictions of the input the factored form no longer shows (`x/x*(x - 1)`: x ≠ 0). */ readonly conditions: readonly Condition[]; };

entries.jsdocSummary: The gcd of two polynomials over ℚ: monic when it has one generator, otherwise with coprime integer coefficients and the term that prints first positive (`x - pi`). Generators include names, π, e and kernels.

entries.signature: export declare function polynomialIn(input: Expr, variable: string, options?: CasOptions): PolynomialIn; ; export declare function polynomialIn(input: CasInput, variable: string, options?: CasOptions): PolynomialIn | CasTextFailure;
entries.jsdocSummary: The input as a polynomial in `variable` with coefficients in ℚ(π, e). It answers a question, so "not a polynomial" is a result, not an error: `rational` gives numerator and denominator coefficients after cancellation, `other` says why and where. Conditions list the divisors the result no longer shows (`x/x - 1` is `[]` with `x ≠ 0`).

entries.name: PolynomialIn

entries.name: simplify
entries.signature: export declare function simplify(input: Expr, options?: CasOptions): SimplifyResult; ; export declare function simplify(input: CasInput, options?: CasOptions): SimplifyResult | CasTextFailure;
entries.jsdocSummary: Simplifies by the rule table of RFC §7 and prints the readable normal form. `conditions` lists every restriction of the input the result no longer shows (reason `domain`) and every caller assumption a rewrite relied on (reason `assumed`). `applied` lists the rule ids that changed something. A string that does not parse returns `parse`'s failure; one the verb cannot handle returns `UnsupportedText`, one over a budget `OverCasBudget`, and one without a value (`x/0`) `NoCasValue`. For an `Expr` the same cases throw.
